title: A test image build could be signed with the production Secure Boot key
description:
schematic-build.yml's test mode (`source_run`) builds a schematic's images from the build inputs of an arbitrary workflow run and signs the UKIs with the production Secure Boot key (the `SECUREBOOT_SIGNING_KEY` secret), the same key nodes' release trust and Secure Boot anchor on. The run is only checked to be numeric, so the inputs could come from a fork PR's `pull_request` run - an outsider's - and the signed result is kept as a downloadable 7-day artifact. With a maintainer dispatching such a build, or the site's workflow-dispatch token, an attacker could obtain a production-signed bundle whose signed command line pins a root filesystem of their choosing, which Install/Upgrade and Secure Boot would accept on every node.

**Affected**: the build pipeline, hence the integrity anchor of every node that installs or updates.

**Fix**: a `source_run` (test) build now signs with a throwaway key generated on the spot, never the production key. Its output is never uploaded to the site and its boot test boots the disk without verifying a signature, so a test key is enough; a production-signed bundle can only come from a release build, whose inputs this repository produced.

**Besides updating**: nothing on nodes; the change is in the CI workflow.
